## When to Use
Use on fresh task-9717fce0 instances with long color-2 lines and nearby patterned marks. Re-derive orientation and alignment from supplied demonstrations before applying the validated behavior.

A 9x27 grid had uniform background 9 and a vertical color-2 line at column 16, rows 0–8. Two color-5 cells were at (row 4,col 15) and (row 5,col 14), forming a diagonal immediately left of the 2-line. Correct output preserved all input cells and added color 8 in a full vertical line at column 13, rows 0–8; nothing else changed. This was accepted as correct.

- Demo 1 (6x23): vertical color-2 line at column 4. A compact, irregular 0 pattern occupied rows 2–3 around columns 8–15. # task-e452cd61: complete the tail of partial horizontal rows

## Validated rule and caution
In the demonstrated orientation, an incomplete horizontal row consists of a same-color run starting at column 0, followed by the ordinary background. Recolor the trailing background cells in that row to color 1. Preserve the original run and all other cells. A complete uniform row of a foreground color stays unchanged; do not recolor it simply because it is a stripe. Re-derive the background, run color, and partial-row positions on each instance.

## Evidence
Demo 1 (10×8): background 9; row 4 is a full row of 3 and remains unchanged. Row 8 is `3 3 3 3 9 9 9 9`; output changes only its suffix to `1 1 1 1`, yielding `3 3 3 3 1 1 1 1`.

Accepted test (15×8): background 6; row 1 is `9 9 9 9 6 6 6 6`; output preserves the first four 9s and changes the background suffix to four 1s. The other rows, including the all-9 row, remain as input.

This supports the left-anchored partial-run completion behavior for these examples. Only one demo pair was available; avoid overgeneralizing to right-anchored runs, multiple runs, other orientations, or different completion colors without fresh evidence."
}
